milestone: M37 External Mode Pack Active Lifecycle

strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Adds explicit Rust-owned replacement of an existing active Mode Pack snapshot with a newly validated local candidate snapshot.
mode.list, mode.get, permission.check, and task.start consume the replacement snapshot after the authorized swap.
Replacement records bounded previous and replacement snapshot summaries without raw Mode Pack JSON or raw ledger payloads.
Headless callers can advance external Mode Pack lifecycle state through replay-safe expected-fingerprint replacement instead of manual state deletion.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances mode_pack_runtime directly, with supporting runtime_permission_enforcement, persistent_structured_ledger, and headless_autonomous_development.
answers.new_capability: The Rust runtime can replace an existing active Mode Pack snapshot with a validated local candidate when the caller supplies explicit authorization and matching expected current and candidate fingerprints.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: modepack.activate intentionally rejects conflicting active snapshots; prior behavior required manual state removal and could not safely advance the active Mode Pack lifecycle.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: External Mode Pack lifecycle remains stuck at first activation, preventing controlled update paths for active external modes.
answers.non_duplicative: Yes. M12.3 added initial activation, while M37.1 adds authorized replacement of an existing active snapshot with stale-current and candidate mismatch protection.
answers.no_new_rpc: No. Existing read RPCs cannot mutate active snapshot state, and modepack.activate preserves no-overwrite activation semantics.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The result carries bounded previous and replacement snapshot summaries as replacement evidence, not a new report/history/digest/readiness wrapper.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: modepack.replaceActive validates authorization, current fingerprint, candidate fingerprint, candidate policy safety, writes the replacement snapshot, records bounded replacement evidence, and makes active-mode consumers use the new snapshot.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Headless callers can update active external Mode Pack policy deterministically and replay the same replacement request without duplicate evidence.
answers.milestone_progress: M37 gains the active Mode Pack replacement transition needed before rollback, remote fetch, and broader lifecycle controls can be considered.

exit_criteria: modepack.replaceActive requires explicit replacement authorization and an existing active snapshot
The runtime rejects stale current activation fingerprints before writing
The runtime rejects candidate activation fingerprint mismatches before writing
The runtime validates and compiles the current .brownie/modepack.json candidate with duplicate built-in mode and unsafe permission rejection before writing
A valid replacement writes one bounded active snapshot and records bounded previous/replacement evidence
Replaying the same replacement returns the same replacement event id and does not append duplicate replacement evidence
mode.list, mode.get, permission.check, and task.start consume the replacement snapshot after success

Ledger, RPC, store, and VSIX payloads contain no raw Mode Pack JSON, prompt, provider response, file content, stdout/stderr, command, environment, raw ledger payload, absolute path, canonical path, or secret
VSIX validators accept valid replacement results and reject malformed fingerprints or raw payload fields

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M37.1 changes product runtime/protocol/store/VSIX behavior and phase manifests; review must confirm this is active snapshot replacement, not another wrapper surface.
